Definition: from ἧλιξ (a comrade, i.e. one of the same age); as big as, i.e. (interjectively) how much:--how (what) great.
BiblicalUsage: Helikos means how great, how large, and it appears twice, both times to measure something unseen. In Colossians 2:1 Paul says he has a great conflict for the churches, how great a conflict, and in James 3:5 the tongue is a little member that boasts great things, and a little fire kindles how great a forest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is a measuring stick for the invisible: a conflict I cannot see, and a fire I cannot put out once the tongue has lit it.
